title: Women, Dalits and Regions in the Freedom Struggle

cards.b: The freedom struggle was not only Congress and Gandhi. Recent UPSC questions ask about women, Dalits, tribes and different regions. This lesson gives you the names.

Women took part from the Swadeshi days. Gandhi’s call brought thousands into picket lines, salt making and jails. Sarojini Naidu (Congress president 1925), Annie Besant (1917), Kasturba Gandhi, Kamala Nehru, Aruna Asaf Ali (hoisted the flag at Gowalia Tank, 1942), Usha Mehta, Sucheta Kripalani, Matangini Hazra, Kanaklata Barua, Captain Lakshmi Sahgal (Rani of Jhansi Regiment, INA).

• Women’s India Association (1917, Besant); National Council of Women (1925); All India Women’s Conference (1927, Margaret Cousins).
  • Pandita Ramabai, Sharada Sadan; Savitribai Phule; Begum Rokeya (Sultana’s Dream, 1905).
  • Bhikaji Cama (Paris, 1907), Madame Cama unfurled a flag at Stuttgart.
  • Rani Gaidinliu (Naga movement), Durgabai Deshmukh and Rani Chennamma earlier.

• Ambedkar: Depressed Classes Conference (1930); Independent Labour Party (1936); Scheduled Castes Federation (1942).
  • Round Table Conferences; Poona Pact (1932).
  • Ayyankali (Kerala, 1893 villuvandi); Mangoo Ram, Ad Dharm movement, Punjab; Jyotirao Phule, Periyar, Iyothee Thass (Tamil).
  • Namasudra movement (Harichand-Guruchand Thakur, Bengal).
Gandhi’s Harijan Sevak Sangh (1932) and Congress temple-entry agitation ran alongside.

Tribal chiefs rose in the 19th century, and later leaders fused with the national cause. Rani Gaidinliu (Heraka movement, Nagaland, 1930s) was jailed by the British; Nehru called her “Rani”. Alluri Sitarama Raju (Rampa, 1922 to 24). Jaipal Singh Munda and the Adivasi Mahasabha (1938) pushed tribal rights. Bhagat Movement among the Oraons (Tana Bhagats, Jatra Bhagat).

• Punjab: Akali Movement (1920s); Gurdwara Reform Act 1925; Ghadar.
  • Kerala: Vaikom, Guruvayur; Malabar rebellion 1921; Punnapra-Vayalar (1946).
  • Tamil Nadu: Vedaranyam march (Rajaji, 1930).
  • Bengal: Chittagong; Tebhaga.
  • Northwest Frontier: Khudai Khidmatgars (Ghaffar Khan).
  • Princely states: All India States’ Peoples Conference (1927), Praja Mandals.

AITUC (1920, Lala Lajpat Rai president), Communist Party (1920s abroad and 1925 Kanpur), Congress Socialist Party (1934; Jayaprakash Narayan, Narendra Dev, Ram Manohar Lohia). Textile strikes (Bombay 1928, Girni Kamgar Union). The Meerut Conspiracy Case (1929) hit the communists.

cards.h: Was it really a mass movement?
cards.b: Subaltern Studies says elite-led nationalism missed the people’s own politics. Feminist scholars (Geraldine Forbes, Radha Kumar) note women took part but stayed within domestic and moral roles in public life. Dalit writers question the Congress’s record on caste. A balanced answer shows both participation and exclusions.

The women’s reservation law, the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam 2023 (106th Amendment), carries this older story. Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (15 November) and rising attention to unsung heroes in the Amrit Mahotsav (2021 to 2023) reflect it. Debates on caste census and social justice are part of the same story.
